<a id="a-configuration-is-how-it-relates--配置由它怎样关系而定"></a>
# A configuration is how it relates

<!-- Generated by tools/research/registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

`configurations-alike-by-relation` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F01 · [record](configurations-alike-by-relation.json) · [register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

> Configurations related by a bisimulation are alike and pass the same tests; a description makes sense where it identifies exactly the alike ones, and carries a law where the frame is determined up to likeness; determinacy as equality depends on names.

<a id="laws--规律"></a>
## Laws

1. Let F and G be frames on configurations S and S′ with the same moves A and claims C. A relation B is a bisimulation between them where related configurations realize the same claims and each step of either is matched by a step of the other by the same move into related configurations; s and s′ are alike where some bisimulation relates them. (`Becoming.Frame`, `Becoming.Bisimulation`, `Becoming.Alike`)
2. Equality is a bisimulation, the converse of a bisimulation is one, and two compose; so likeness is reflexive, symmetric and transitive, stated as a relation since a quotient needs Quot.sound. (`Becoming.Bisimulation.eq`, `Becoming.Bisimulation.converse`, `Becoming.Bisimulation.comp`, `Becoming.Alike.refl`, `Becoming.Alike.symm`, `Becoming.Alike.trans`)
3. Alike configurations realize the same claims, match each other's steps by the same move into alike configurations and every course of moves into alike configurations, and pass the same tests, a course of moves followed by a claim. (`Becoming.Alike.realized`, `Becoming.Alike.step`, `Becoming.Bisimulation.trace`, `Becoming.Alike.trace`, `Becoming.Alike.tests`)
4. A frame is determined up to likeness at s where any two outcomes of one move at s are alike; a determined frame is so everywhere; determinacy up to likeness passes along likeness, and where it holds the same move takes alike configurations to alike ones. (`Becoming.Determined`, `Becoming.DeterminedAt`, `Becoming.Determined.at`, `Becoming.DeterminedAt.transfer`, `Becoming.DeterminedAt.goAlike`)
5. In Twins a start has two successors by one move: they are alike, the frame is not determined, and its start is alike to the start of a frame with one successor, which is determined, so the twins are determined up to likeness at the start. (`Becoming.Twins.Config`, `Becoming.Twins.frame`, `Becoming.Twins.one`, `Becoming.Twins.not_determined`, `Becoming.Twins.one_determined`, `Becoming.Twins.bisimulation`, `Becoming.Twins.left_alike_right`, `Becoming.Twins.successor_not_start`, `Becoming.Twins.bisimulation_one`, `Becoming.Twins.alike_one`)
6. Under the law of exchange read through the claims that a relatum stands at an amount, agreeing at every relatum is a bisimulation; standings are alike exactly where they agree at every relatum, and the law is determined up to likeness at every standing. (`Becoming.exchangeFrame`, `Becoming.exchange_pointwise_bisimulation`, `Becoming.exchange_alike_of_pointwise`, `Becoming.exchange_pointwise_of_alike`, `Becoming.exchange_alike_iff`, `Becoming.exchange_determinedAt`)
7. A description π of configurations makes sense where it identifies exactly the alike configurations; it does exactly where being identified by it is a bisimulation and it identifies every alike pair; descriptions that make sense identify the same configurations. (`Becoming.IdentifiesAlike`, `Becoming.identifiesAlike_iff`, `Becoming.IdentifiesAlike.unique`)
8. Where the frame is determined up to likeness everywhere, a description that makes sense carries a law (through carries_law_iff of Becoming.Mechanism); naming the configurations makes sense exactly where alike configurations are one, and the twins' naming does not. (`Becoming.FactorsThrough`, `Becoming.carries_law_iff`, `Becoming.IdentifiesAlike.carries`, `Becoming.identifiesAlike_id_iff`, `Becoming.Twins.naming_not_identifiesAlike`)
9. For a determined law read through a map, the claims being the map's value, configurations are alike exactly where their futures through the map are the same, and there a description that makes sense carries a law. (`Becoming.Law.orbit`, `Becoming.Law.orbit_shift`, `Becoming.Law.process`, `Becoming.Law.frameBy`, `Becoming.Law.frameBy_determined`, `Becoming.Law.SameFuture`, `Becoming.Law.alike_future`, `Becoming.Law.sameFuture_bisimulation`, `Becoming.Law.alike_iff_sameFuture`, `Becoming.Law.IdentifiesAlike.carries`)
10. In the periphery bridge, Deeper.Bisimulation of RelationalDynamics is the core's bisimulation of frames with no claims, so in static and toggle every configuration of one is alike to every configuration of the other. (`Becoming.Frame.bare`, `Becoming.deeper_bisimulation_iff`, `Becoming.static_toggle_alike`)
11. In the periphery bridge, ExplanatoryBranching.Bisimulation is the core's bisimulation of frames whose claims are a model's conditions, and alike configurations pass every branching test, negation and conjunction included (through bisimulation_implies_same). (`Becoming.Frame.ofModel`, `Becoming.branching_bisimulation_iff`, `Becoming.Alike.same`)

<a id="conditions--条件"></a>
## Conditions

- No premise: likeness is characterized by bisimulation, not assumed, and no quotient is taken; Alike.tests, exchange_alike_iff, identifiesAlike_iff and identifiesAlike_id_iff are two-way.
- Bisimulation compares frames with the same move and claim types; a test is a claim after a finite course of moves, and the conditions under which passing the same tests makes configurations alike are given by tests-fix-likeness-where-determined.
- Determinacy up to likeness (DeterminedAt) is a definition; the Part I theorems stated with Determined are restated with it in determinacy-up-to-likeness.
- IdentifiesAlike.carries needs the frame determined up to likeness at every configuration; a description that makes sense is supplied, and that one exists is not derived.
- For the witnesses: the frames of Twins, and the law of exchange read through exchangeFrame.

<a id="does-not-show--未表明"></a>
## Does not show

- That configurations passing the same tests are alike is not stated here; its conditions are in tests-fix-likeness-where-determined.
- That a description making sense exists is not stated: describing each configuration by what it is alike to makes sense given function and propositional extensionality, and the quotient by likeness needs Quot.sound.
- Likeness takes no quotient, so “alike configurations are one and the same” is not stated here.
- **Counterexample:** Determinacy as equality depends on names: in Twins the two successors are alike in every relation, the frame is not determined, and it is alike to a determined frame (Twins.not_determined, Twins.left_alike_right, Twins.alike_one). [source](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Unfolding.lean)

<a id="correspondence--对应"></a>
### Correspondence

Following Ren's “yes, put it on the board and start”: the split “configurations prior to their relation” stated from the world's side. It brings into the core the periphery's relational identity of configurations (RelationalDynamics, 6 October 2026; the branching tests of ExplanatoryBranching). There a step leaving the configuration unchanged was found to read the carrier's equality (unchanged_reads_carrier_identity); so does determinacy as equality (Twins). Readings (the AI's; Ren agreed): the names of configurations, like those of relata (Becoming.Identity), carry nothing, and what can be found out is the same for alike configurations; under the law of exchange, agreeing at every relatum is being alike, so the zero-premise plan's commitment to pointwise properties in place of function extensionality (§1.2, b(5)) states the relational identity of standings, function extensionality adding only that alike standings are one and the same. Descriptions that make sense restate on this module's definitions, for frames that branch and carry claims, the IdentifiesAlike checked for one determined law on the branch "Current math core (fork)" (its Saying.lean, answering Ren's questions on framing and pairs).

The converse (passing the same tests gives a bisimulation) is given classically in the periphery for image-finite models by same_iff_bisimilar, and constructively in the core on finite decided frames (alike_iff_sameBranchingTests of Becoming.Likeness); the core's branching tests correspond one to one to the periphery's (sameBranchingTests_iff_same in the bridge), so on finite decided models the periphery's same tests are likeness with no classical reasoning (same_iff_alike_of_finiteDecided).
  - Output: Branching tests and bisimulation; bisimulation gives the same tests.
  - Input: The core's likeness passing all of the periphery's branching tests.

- related, not a proved adapter: [becoming-spine-instances](becoming-spine-instances.md). The bridge module: the periphery's interfaces are instances of the spine; the periphery's two bisimulations become the core's there.
- related, not a proved adapter: [tests-fix-likeness-where-determined](tests-fix-likeness-where-determined.md). The conditions under which tests fix likeness: both frames determined up to likeness for linear tests, both finite and decided for branching tests.
